chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-'Abbas, from Sa'dan, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
I heard him saying: “Whoever seeks a need while he is not in a state of wudu (ablution), and it is not fulfilled, then he should blame none but himself.”

key_terms.حَاجَةً: a need or request that a person seeks to have fulfilled
key_terms.غَيْرِ وُضُوءٍ: without being in a state of ritual ablution

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about seeking one's needs without wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the merit of being in a state of wudu (ablution) when seeking one’s needs. It presents wudu (ablution) as part of proper spiritual etiquette and indicates that neglecting it may be a cause for not attaining what one seeks.
